title: Dredged Material Containment Area (DMCA) O&M Construction IDC
agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE > DEPT OF THE ARMY > USACE > SAD > W074 ENDIST SAVANNAH
description:
Purpose:   The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Savannah District, is seeking information from industry to determine the availability and capability of qualified contractors is to provide general construction for the new construction, rehabilitation, replacement, repair, and construction-related maintenance of Dredged Material Containment Areas (DMCAs) and associated infrastructure within Savannah and Brunswick Harbors. All work shall be performed in a safe, timely, and cost-effective manner. 

 This notice is issued for the purpose of conducting market research.  This is not a Solicitation Announcement, nor is it a Request for Proposal.  

 The Government is contemplating a potential acquisition strategy.  The results of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. 

 The Government is seeking to identify capable firms, including small businesses, that have recent and relevant experience in performing DMCA-related construction work, such as site preparation, dike construction and repair, weir/structure rehabilitation, erosion control, grading, and general access improvements. 

 Task orders will be executed using the Design-Bid-Build (DBB) delivery method. The Contractor will perform construction in accordance with Government-furnished designs. 

   Requirements:   Work under this contract is restricted to the designated DMCAs, bird islands, and directly associated supporting infrastructure located within the Savannah and Brunswick Harbor operational footprints: 

 
	 Savannah Harbor Facilities: Disposal Areas 1N, 2A, 12A, 13A, 13B, 14A, and 14B; Jones/Oysterbed Island (JOI); and associated bird islands. 
	 Brunswick Harbor Facilities: Andrews Island DMCA. 
 

 The Government anticipates awarding a Firm-Fixed Price Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Construction Contract with an expected effective date in late FY27 – early FY28. The anticipated contract period of performance is five (5) years. The contract will provide for the construction, rehabilitation, replacement, repair, and construction-related maintenance of Dredged Material Containment Areas (DMCAs) and associated infrastructure within Savannah and Brunswick Harbors. All work shall be performed in a safe, timely, and cost-effective manner in accordance with the requirements of this contract and individual task orders. 

 The Contractor shall furnish all necessary supervision, labor, materials, equipment, transportation, temporary facilities, construction quality control, and other resources required to complete construction activities under individual task orders in accordance with the applicable contract requirements. 

 Individual task orders will establish specific work limits, requirements, and completion criteria. 

 Task orders will be issued based on the Government’s requirements and may specify performance durations (e.g., calendar days). 

  Representative construction and maintenance tasks may include, but are not limited to  construction, rehabilitation, repair, and maintenance of designated DMCA infrastructure, including dikes, embankments, roads, access areas, drainage and water-control systems, shoreline protection, marine access features, and associated structural, mechanical, and electrical components. Supporting activities may include earthwork, excavation, material handling, dewatering, vegetation and debris removal, erosion control, site restoration, surveys, utility protection, temporary facilities, waterborne access, testing, and documentation necessary to complete authorized task orders. All work shall comply with applicable environmental, material handling, disposal, seasonal, and access requirements. General building construction and HVAC work are excluded. 

   Interested Firms:   

 If you are interested in this contract and/or your firm has the potential capacity to perform these requirements, please provide the following information by  27 Nov 2026 . 

 •   Complete the following survey using the link:
